title: introduce-perf-mode-and-aria-announcements-for-large-timeseries
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design and propose a charting UX pattern that exposes a lightweight 'Performance mode' toggle for time-series components and implements ARIA announcement behavior for large, frequently-updating series. Goal: ship a pattern that maintains interactive fidelity for small datasets while offering a predictable, low-latency fallback for heavy traces and noisy real-time feeds. Also align color/spacing tokens and provide implementation guidance for Canvas vs SVG rendering paths.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens used consistently (color/line-width/spacing) with a migration map for legacy charts
A documented Performance mode toggle with clear default behaviors for Canvas vs SVG implementations
ARIA announcement strategy defined: when to announce, summary phrasing, and rate-limiting to avoid screen reader spam
Prototype in Figma + simple interactive demo (Canvas) demonstrating mode switch and accessibility announcements
Design spec includes guidelines for downsampling/decimation strategies and recommended heuristics for switching modes
comments: 2026-02-25 Maya Patel: Initial ticket created after Research Sync. Observed several customer dashboards with >2000 series samples causing jank. Proposal: two-mode UX — 'High fidelity' (default for small series) and 'Performance' (aggressive decimation + aggregated tooltip summaries).

2026-02-27 Javier Morales: Quick spike with engineering showed Canvas path yields 3-4x less CPU on stress traces. Need design tokens mapping for line thickness when switching modes (thin in perf mode to reduce overdraw).

2026-03-02 Anika Bose (a11y): Screen reader noise is a real risk. Recommend use of aria-live polite + batching announcements every 2s with a one-line summary e.g., 'CPU: 3 series updated, latest range 12–78%'. Avoid announcing raw values for every sample.

2026-03-04 Design review notes: PM wants an opt-out for customers who rely on exact data semantics. Add a per-chart prop 'explicitMode' to lock mode. Also capture guidance for legends: virtualize legend items and provide keyboard-driven search when series count > 50.

2026-03-06 Engineering feedback (ENG-4120): Kernel-level batching for real-time feeds will help. For perf-mode default decimation, suggest simple largest-triangle-three-buckets (LTTB) with tunable bucket size. Need a documented API surface: decimationThreshold sample count, mode defaults, ariaSummaryFormatter callback.

2026-03-08 UX iteration: wireframes updated in Figma to include a small mode pill in top-right of chart. Tooltip behavior in perf-mode summarized: show aggregated metrics (min/median/max) and list collapsed top-3 series by contribution. Added microcopy for onboarding: 'Performance mode reduces detail to keep charts responsive.'

2026-03-10 PM review (Liam Chen): Approve direction. Please add a migration checklist for existing charts that rely on the old tooltip-per-point semantics. Ops asked for toggle to persist per-user in the Console settings; logged as follow-up ENG-4209.

2026-03-12 Design handoff: Final spec link uploaded to Confluence. Included token mapping table (chart.tokens) and react prop examples. Requesting engineering estimate for implementation on Canvas path + light fallback for SVG within 2-week sprint.
design_notes: Performance mode should prioritize frame time under 16ms for 60FPS dashboards; target 30–60ms frame time reduction compared to high-fidelity mode on stress fixtures.
Use a single aria-live region per chart. Announce a compact summary and expose a keyboard shortcut (press 'A' when chart focused) to read the last N datapoints in detail.
Tooltip: in perf-mode, present aggregated values and offer 'Expand details' action that temporarily lifts decimation for hovered window (500ms grace period).
Legend: collapse low-contributing series under a 'More' disclosure after 30 items; provide client-side virtualization with accessible focus management.
implementation_guidance: Canvas preferred for >1000 points; SVG is acceptable for <=1000 with virtualization. Use requestAnimationFrame for render loops and avoid synchronous layout thrashing.
Provide a native decimation util (LTTB) in the charting library with deterministic output for snapshots/tests.
ARIA patterns: single aria-live polite region; aria-roledescription='time series chart'; role='region' with accessible name from chart title.

Accessibility review session with a11y team and keyboard users — schedule for 2026-03-17
